'''Andre Devon Brown''' (born May 12, 1981) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for [[DePaul University]] and went on to play professionally in Europe, Asia, South America, Australia, and in the [[National Basketball Association]] and the [[NBA Development League]]. He is also a former two-year member of the USA Basketball World Youth Games team that won a gold medal 1998 and a bronze medal in 1999.

==High school career==
As a high school freshman, Brown attended [[Brother Rice High School (Chicago)|Brother Rice High School]] in his hometown of [[Chicago]]. As a sophomore, he transferred to nearby [[Leo Catholic High School]] where he led his new team downstate and along the way, captured Class A All-State honors, being the only sophomore on the ballot. The following year Leo moved up in population and therefore changed classes to the larger Class AA. In Class AA, Brown continued his dominating ways, garnering All-State honors again, this time initiating the record as the only player to ever be both Class A and AA All-State. Things were changed up again for his senior year in 1999–2000 as Leo were moved back down to Class A,<ref>[http://highschoolelite.com/tournaments/classastate.html HighSchoolElite.com's Class A All-State]</ref> as Brown went on to help Leo win the Catholic League title and earn [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] honors.<ref>[https://www.chicagotribune.com/2000/02/19/leo-rips-brother-rice-for-catholic-crown/ Leo Rips Brother Rice For Catholic Crown]</ref>

==College career==
In his freshman season at [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]], Brown joined Imari Sawyer as the first DePaul newcomers since 1992 to have a double-double in their first collegiate game, as he recorded 18 points and 11 rebounds against [[Lewis University]]. He scored a season-high 19 points while also grabbing eight rebounds against Marquette. In 30 games (six starts), he averaged 6.5 points and 4.9 rebounds in 22.6 minutes per game.<ref name=bio>[http://www.nba.com/draft2004/profiles/AndreBrown.html Prospect Profile: Andre Brown]</ref><ref name=stats>[https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/andre-brown-1.html Andre Brown Stats]</ref>

In his sophomore season, Brown became the first DePaul player since Stanley Brundy in 1988–89 to lead the team in scoring, rebounding, field goal percentage and blocked shots. He also ranked among Conference USA leaders for rebounding (second), scoring (13th) and field goal percentage (14th). He set a C-USA single game record with 27 rebounds against TCU, which was the second-best single-game total in DePaul history. In 26 games (25 starts), he averaged 14.5 points, 9.4 rebounds and 1.0 blocks in 31.8 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

In his junior season, Brown was selected to the Preseason All-Conference USA team by the league coaches, and went on to record multiple double-doubles in 2002–03, none better than a game-high 20 points and 11 rebounds against UNLV. In 28 games (18 starts), he averaged 9.4 points and 9.0 rebounds in 30.5 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

In his senior season, Brown earned second-team All-Conference USA honors after he was first selected to the Conference USA All-Preseason team and during the season, he was twice named C-USA Player of the Week. He was also named to the All-Tournament team at the Spartan Coca-Cola Classic. In 23 games (all starts), he averaged 13.5 points and 9.2 rebounds in 32.2 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

Brown finished his four-year career ranked fourth in Conference USA history with 855 rebounds and became one of only eight players in DePaul history to have 1,000 points and 800 rebounds in a career. He went on to be named to the All-Tournament Team at the 2004 Portsmouth Invitational Tournament after averaging 18.3 points (4th in tourney) and 10.7 rebounds (2nd in tourney).<ref name="bio" />

==Professional career==

===2004–05 season===
After going undrafted in the [[2004 NBA draft]], Brown joined the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] for the 2004 [[NBA Summer League]]. On October 4, 2004, he signed with the [[New Jersey Nets]]. However, he was later waived by the Nets on October 20, 2004.<ref name=nets>[http://www.nba.com/nets/news/Training_Camp_Release_100924.html Nets Announce Training Camp Roster]</ref> The following month, he signed with [[Roseto Sharks|Sedima Roseto]] of Italy for the 2004–05 season. In February 2005, he left Roseto and signed with [[KK Budućnost Podgorica|Budućnost Podgorica]] of Montenegro for the rest of the season. In April 2005, he joined the [[Barangay Ginebra San Miguel|Barangay Ginebra Kings]] of the Philippines where he played seven games for the club before leaving in late May.<ref>[http://www.arabnews.com/node/266238 Ritualo Helps FedEx Past Red Bull; Aces Demolish Gin Kings]</ref>

===2005–06 season===
In July 2005, Brown joined the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] for the 2005 NBA Summer League. In October 2005, he signed with the [[Goyang Orions|Daegu Orions]] of South Korea for the 2005–06 season.<ref>[http://depaul.scout.com/story/457439-andre-brown-playing-in-south-korea ANDRE BROWN PLAYING IN SOUTH KOREA]</ref> In February 2006, he was traded to the [[Incheon Electroland Elephants|Incheon ET Land Black Slamer]].

===2006–07 season===
In July 2006, Brown joined the [[San Antonio Spurs]] for the 2006 NBA Summer League. On September 29, 2006, he signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/Camp_PR_092906.html Hawks Add Six To Training Camp Roster]</ref> However, he was later waived by the Hawks on October 26, 2006.<ref>[http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/180296/Hawks_Waive_Glyniadakis_And_Brown Hawks Waive Glyniadakis And Brown]</ref> On November 2, 2006, he was selected by the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] with the second overall pick in the [[2006 NBA Development League Draft]]. He went on to earn D-League Player of the Week honors on December 18 after recording three straight double-doubles over the week as he led the Skyforce to a 3–0 record.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/performer_061218.html D-League Performer of the Week, December 18, 2006] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090501170742/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/performer_061218.html |date=May 1, 2009 }}</ref> In 16 games for Sioux Falls, he averaged 22.8 points and 10.8 rebounds per game.

On January 5, 2007, Brown signed a 10-day contract with the Seattle SuperSonics, going on to sign a second 10-day contract on February 15, and for the rest of the season on January 25.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/nba_news/sonics_brown_070125.html Sonics Sign Andre Brown for Rest of the Season]</ref><ref>[http://www.seattlepi.com/news/article/Impressed-Sonics-sign-Brown-for-rest-of-season-1226482.php Impressed Sonics sign Brown for rest of season]</ref>

===2007–08 season===
Despite joining the [[Indiana Pacers]] but not playing for them during the 2007 NBA Summer League, Brown signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] on July 20, 2007.<ref>[http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/2007-07-20-743128518_x.htm Memphis Grizzlies sign forward Andre Brown]</ref> Despite a promising stint with the SuperSonics, Brown managed just 33 games for Memphis in 2007–08 as he averaged 3.0 points and 2.8 rebounds in 8.7 minutes per game. He did, however, average 13.0 points and 11.5 rebounds in 27.8 minutes per game over the final four games of the season after the Grizzlies had already been ruled out of playoff contention.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/brownan01/gamelog/2008/ Andre Brown 2007–08 Game Log]</ref>

===2008–09 season===
On September 28, 2008, Brown signed with the [[Charlotte Bobcats]].<ref>[http://archive.digtriad.com/news/story.aspx?storyid=111495 Bobcats Add Brown, Williams, Taylor To Roster] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304001820/http://archive.digtriad.com/news/story.aspx?storyid=111495 |date=2016-03-04 }}</ref> However, he was later waived by the Bobcats on November 19, 2008, after appearing in four regular season games.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3713885 Bobcats try to boost frontcourt with moves, pursuit of McDyess]</ref> On December 3, he was acquired by the [[Austin Toros]] of the NBA Development League. On January 22, he parted ways with Austin after appearing in 17 games.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/transactions_08-09.html 2008–09 Transactions] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151219004752/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/transactions_08-09.html |date=December 19, 2015 }}</ref> A few days later, he signed with [[Banvit B.K.|Banvit Bandırma]] of Turkey for the rest of the [[2008–09 Turkish Basketball League|season]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/75039/andre-brown-is-coming-to-turkey.html Andre Brown is coming to Turkey]</ref>

===2009–10 season===
In July 2009, Brown joined the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for the 2009 NBA Summer League. On December 3, 2009, he signed with the [[Zhejiang Golden Bulls]] for the rest of the [[2009–10 CBA season]].<ref name=sham>{{Cite web |url=http://data.shamsports.com/content/pages/data/world/transactions/2010.jsp |title=General basketball transactions: 2009/10 |access-date=2014-12-16 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20141108160715/http://data.shamsports.com/content/pages/data/world/transactions/2010.jsp |archive-date=2014-11-08 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On April 1, 2010, Brown signed with [[Leones de Ponce (basketball)|Leones de Ponce]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] where he played one game before signing with [[Jalaa SC (men's basketball)|Al Jalaa Aleppo]] of Syria on April 22 for the rest of the season.<ref name="sham" />

===2010–11 season===
In July 2010, Brown joined the [[Golden State Warriors]] for the 2010 NBA Summer League.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ridiculousupside.com/2010/6/28/1540775/nba-summer-league-rosters-vegas |title=NBA Summer League Rosters – Vegas |access-date=June 30, 2010 |archive-date=October 21, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151021193042/http://www.ridiculousupside.com/2010/6/28/1540775/nba-summer-league-rosters-vegas |url-status=dead }}</ref> On September 24, 2010, he signed with the New Jersey Nets, re-joining the team for a second stint.<ref name="nets" /> However, much like last time, he was waived by the team on September 29, before training camp even began.<ref>[http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/206645/Nets-Waive-Andre-Brown-From-Training-Camp-Roster Nets Waive Andre Brown From Training Camp Roster]</ref> Five days later, he signed a one-year deal with [[Panellinios B.C.]] of the [[Greek Basket League]].<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20141217164427/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/home/transactions/eurocup-2010-11/i/76413/4674/panellinios-picks-up-big-man-brown|title=PANELLINIOS picks up big man Brown}}</ref> On January 6, 2011, he was released by Panellinios after appearing in six league games and three EuroCup games.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://data.shamsports.com/content/pages/data/world/transactions/2011.jsp |title=General basketball transactions: 2010/11 |access-date=2014-12-16 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20141108160716/http://data.shamsports.com/content/pages/data/world/transactions/2011.jsp |archive-date=2014-11-08 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On January 13, 2011, Brown signed with the [[Perth Wildcats]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] as a short-term injury replacement for [[Matthew Knight (basketball)|Matthew Knight]].<ref>[https://au.news.yahoo.com/thewest/sport/a/8641772/wildcats-sign-ex-nba-big-man-brown/ Wildcats sign ex-NBA big man Brown]</ref><ref>[https://au.news.yahoo.com/thewest/sport/basketball/a/8663764/wildcats-import-in-it-for-the-long-haul/ Wildcats import in it for the long haul]</ref> However, after losing co-captain [[Shawn Redhage]] to a season-ending hip injury on January 23,<ref>[https://au.news.yahoo.com/thewest/sport/basketball/a/8698418/redhage-ruled-out-for-season/ Redhage ruled out for season]</ref><ref>[https://au.news.yahoo.com/thewest/a/8707886/wildcats-weigh-brown-extension/ Wildcats weigh up Brown extension]</ref> Brown's contract was extended by the Wildcats to see out the [[2010–11 NBL season|2010–11 season]].<ref>[https://au.news.yahoo.com/thewest/sport/a/8737649/hard-man-brown-heeds-call-to-stay/ Hard-man Brown heeds call to stay]</ref> The Wildcats went on to finish fourth on the ladder and played the [[New Zealand Breakers]] in the semi-finals, where they lost 2 games to 1. In 15 games for the Wildcats, he averaged 9.3 points and 6.7 rebounds per game.<ref>[http://www.foxsportspulse.com/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&pID=192078261&client=0-189-12314-119318-369909 Player statistics for Andre Brown]</ref>

===2011–12 season===
On July 7, 2011, Brown signed with Huracanes del Atlántico for the 2011 [[Liga Nacional de Baloncesto|LNB]] season.<ref>[http://www.dominicanosenbasket.com/2011/07/lnb-huracanes-del-atlantico-contratan.html LNB – HURACANES DEL ATLANTICO CONTRATAN EX NBA ANDRE BROWN] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304045544/http://www.dominicanosenbasket.com/2011/07/lnb-huracanes-del-atlantico-contratan.html |date=March 4, 2016 }} {{in lang|es}}</ref>

On November 10, 2011, Brown signed with [[Shahrdari Gorgan BC|Shahrdari Gorgan]] of Iran for the 2011–12 season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://data.shamsports.com/content/pages/data/world/transactions/2012.jsp |title=General basketball transactions: 2011/12 |access-date=2014-12-16 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20141104075734/http://data.shamsports.com/content/pages/data/world/transactions/2012.jsp |archive-date=2014-11-04 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===2012–13 season===
On October 14, 2012, Brown signed with the [[Jeonju KCC Egis|KCC Egis]] of South Korea for the 2012–13 season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://data.shamsports.com/content/pages/data/world/transactions/2013.jsp |title=General basketball transactions: 2012/13 |access-date=December 16, 2014 |archive-date=May 13, 2014 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140513090700/http://data.shamsports.com/content/pages/data/world/transactions/2013.jsp |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===2013–14 season===
On November 14, 2013, Brown signed with Club Atlético Atenas of Uruguay for the 2013–14 season.<ref>[http://www.futbol.com.uy/auc.aspx?218812 Algo se acordará] {{in lang|es}}</ref> However, he left the club later that month after just two games.

On January 24, 2014, Brown signed with the [[Sendai 89ers]] of Japan for the rest of the season.<ref>[http://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2014/01/24/basketball/bj-league/former-nba-forward-andre-brown-joins-sendai-89ers/ Former NBA forward Andre Brown joins Sendai 89ers]</ref> However, less than a week later, he parted ways with the club before playing in a game for them after a family emergency arose.<ref>[http://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2014/02/01/basketball/bj-league/ex-nba-player-brown-parts-ways-with-sendai-due-to-family-emergency/ Ex-NBA player Brown parts ways with Sendai due to family emergency]</ref> He went on to sign with [[Al-Ahli Club (Manama)|Al-Ahli]] of Bahrain on February 26 for the rest of the season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/112160/al-ahli-manama-sign-andre-brown.html Al Ahli Manama sign Andre Brown]</ref><ref>[http://www.court-side.com/news/blog/andre-brown-links-al-ahli/ Andre Brown links with Al Ahli]</ref>
